Good morning. Oil prices have climbed above $108 a barrel after a series of drone attacks from Iraq’s territory forced Saudi Arabia to close its east-west crude pipeline. Saudi traders said the kingdom would run out of oil stocks for export if it did not reopen within days. Gas prices also climbed higher. The spike came as the Iran-aligned Houthi forces in Yemen launched several attacks against Saudi Arabia and captured the strategic island of Perim in the Bab al-Mandab strait on Sunday, expanding their control of the waterway.

Where did the attack on Saudi Arabia come from? Iraq’s government confirmed the attacks were launched from its territory and ordered an investigation. Baghdad is under mounting pressure to stop militant groups – including those backed by Saudi Arabia’s regional rival Iran – launching attacks on Gulf countries from Iraqi soil. The US president, Donald Trump, said he believed Tehran was responsible.

Why has Saudi Arabia been relying on its east-west pipeline? Riyadh has increased the use of the 745-mile pipeline since the start of the war on Iran in order to bypass the strait of Hormuz’s closure. The world’s biggest exporter has used the pipeline to reroute about 4m barrels a day – about 4% of global supply – but with the ‌pipeline out of service, the Red Sea port of Yanbu now has stocks to maintain exports for just five to seven days.

What is the Anthropic CEO proposing? Robert Booth explains Amodei’s suggestion: first, each US AI company grants access to third-party evaluators; second, all companies in democratic countries establish common safety standards; and third, the world’s democratic AI powers coordinate with autocracies – notably China – to control the race.

events.title: Hungary begins hunt for corrupt regime's billions

events.title: Croatia: Toxic waste protest draws tens of thousands
events.summary: The Zagreb demonstrators demanded that the government come up with a plan to clear illegal toxic waste in 20 days. Prime Minister Plenkovic has promised to tackle the issue.

events.title: Germany: From emigration to immigration destination

events.title: Germany news: Thousands march at Saxony-Anhalt rallies

events.title: Outrage as Maltese tycoon acquitted in journalist's murder

events.title: In Saxony-Anhalt election, small parties will be kingmakers

events.title: Why North Korea's women's football team is so good

events.title: Austria women ice hockey team fight for future generations

events.title: EU summons Russian envoy over failed Leipzig drone attack

events.summary: One of Germany's top footballers has collapsed on the pitch for a second time in four days ahead of the new season. Bayern Munich's Jamal Musiala has said he has a "neurological dysfunction" that causes blackouts.

events.summary: Five countries border the Caspian Sea, but none owns a fixed share. A 2018 convention established rules for navigation, security and fishing while leaving some seabed borders unresolved.

events.title: In drought-stricken France, tankers supply drinking water
events.summary: France is seeing water shortages in regions that usually have plenty of supply. This summer's extreme heat is exposing how unprepared much of the country, and Europe, is for increasing water scarcity.

events.summary: Germany's main farmers' association has warned of a below-average harvest after drought and crops damaged by extreme heat. DW looks into what lower yields could mean for food prices and grocery bills.

events.summary: Inside futuristic labs, plants are scanned, stressed and analyzed. The aim is to use the results to produce plant strains that can better serve a growing population in a warming world.

events.summary: Wildfires destroy lives and livelihoods. But survivors and firefighters also suffer long-term harm to their health. A growing body of research suggests particulate matter (PM2.5) in wildfire smoke is a major culprit.

events.title: Norway wealth fund sounds alarm on AI stock market bubble
events.summary: The head of Norway's sovereign wealth fund has warned that soaring AI-driven stock valuations could trigger a sharp correction. How exposed is the world's largest sovereign wealth fund to a market downturn?

events.title: 'What makes China work despite the pain in society?' asks analyst Dan Wang
events.summary: In this edition of Perspective, FRANCE 24’s Stuart Norval speaks to Dan Wang, a China expert whose book ‘Breakneck:  China’s Quest to Engineer the Future’ is a New York Times bestseller. It takes a close look at Chinese life and draws from Wang’s own ten years of living there. Wang says the China and the US are some of the most similar people in the world, as they are both hustlers and take shortcuts.

events.title: French 2027 presidential elections: Why Gen Z has mobilised for Mélenchon
events.summary:
🇫🇷 French far-left presidential candidate Jean-Luc #Mélenchon is both highly controversial and a #GenZ favourite.
 
Mélenchon's young supporters express admiration for his promises to stage a "citizen's revolution",  redistrubute wealth, fight #climatechange and support #Palestine. The candidate's critics have accused him of complancency towards #Russia and antisemitism. 
 
Despite being divisive, recent polls predict that Mélenchon will qualify for the second round of #France's 2027 presidential #election, where he would likely face far-right candidate Marine #LePen.
 
So, why has France's Gen Z mobilised for Mélenchon?
 
🔴 FRANCE 24's Gabrielle Nadler spoke to young voters to find out.

events.title: Should the brakes be put on AI?
events.summary: US President Donald Trump says he is worried about America giving China an edge in the Artificial Intelligence market if too many rules and regulations are put on it. In recent days industry insiders, including top executives at Open AI and Anthropic, have once again sounded the alarm, saying that the way AI is being developed could threaten humanity and calling for more checks to be put in place.

events.title: Trump criticises 'negative forces' seeking to slow AI development
events.summary: US President Donald Trump on Sunday slammed critics of artificial intelligence (AI) who warned firms to slow down development, branding them "negative" forces. The comments came soon after OpenAI CEO Sam Altman announced his company will not go public this year, citing safety concerns.

events.title: Climate catastrophe leaves Nepal mourning while the search for the missing continues
events.summary: The himalayan flash flood that devastated northern Nepal on August 26 was an unprecedented disaster. The death toll continues to rise, with nearly 1,400 people now confirmed dead and 5,130 still missing, including around 600 foreign nationals from 35 countries.

events.title: Was Russian train strike meant to 'scare' the West?
events.summary: The EU's top diplomat said Monday that Russian strikes which hit a Warsaw-bound train near Ukraine's border with Poland shortly after top Western figures passed through were meant to "scare" off Kyiv's backers. France 24's correspondent in Kyiv, Gulliver Cragg, has the latest.

events.title: Russia strikes Ukraine with drones as Poland warns of 'escalation'
events.summary: Russia continues its ramped-up air campaign against Ukraine, launching 453 drones in an overnight blitz. One drone struck 800 metres from a border crossing with Poland prompting the polish military to scramble fighter jets and helicopters.

events.title: Thousands rally in support of Brazil's Lula as election campaigning heats up
events.summary: With Brazil set to hold a Presidential election on October 4th, supporters of both incumbent Luiz Inacio Lula Da Silva and his main opponent Flavio Bolsonaro have been taking to the streets. Polls have the candidates, who are on opposite ends of political spectrum, neck and neck.

events.title: Dozens arrested as Turkish police raid LGBTQ bars, activists' homes
events.summary: Turkish police on Sunday made dozens of arrests in a slew of raids on gay bars and the homes of LGBTQ activists. Authorities said the raids came in the context of the "Decade of the Family" proclaimed by Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan, aimed at "protecting our children, the institution of the family and social order".

events.title: A 'complicated autumn' awaits Sweden after knife-edge vote
events.summary: Sweden's general election remained too close to call early Monday, with nearly 90 percent of votes counted. Four opposition parties led by Social Democrat Magdalena Andersson held a one-seat parliamentary lead over Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson's right-wing bloc, which includes the Sweden Democrats, as both leaders said they were ready to govern.

events.title: ‘They drove us from our land’: Thousands displaced by Yemen conflict
events.summary: According to the UN, more than 86,000 people have been displaced in Yemen since July, following fighting between the Iran-backed Houthis rebels and government forces. Many have fled to refugee camps in government-controlled Aden, while others have headed to neighbouring Djibouti.

events.title: Yemen govt forces hit back as conflict with Houthis intensifies
events.summary: The conflict in Yemen intensified on Sunday, as government forces launched attacks against Iran-backed Houthi rebels along the Red Sea and Houthis fired into neighboring Saudi Arabia, which supports Yemen’s government. The Yemeni government vowed to send more forces to the Red Sea coast and one official conceded a “painful” defeat last week when Houthis captured the port city of Mokha and an island on the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, a crucial shipping alternative to the Strait of Hormuz.

events.title: 'Palpable tension' as Philippines Muslim region holds first elections
events.summary: A predominantly Muslim region in the southern Philippines held its first parliamentary elections on Monday, seen as a crucial step in the long quest for self-rule after decades of insurgency and violence. Reporting from the region, France 24’s look Jan Camenzind Broomby, takes a look at the vote’s significance, as well as the tensions surrounding election day.

events.title: Retrial over 2018 France terror attack begins
events.summary: The retrial of three defendants linked to a 2018 terror attack in a supermarket in southern France that left four people dead begins in Paris on Monday. The defendants include the former partner of the attacker himself, who was shot dead by the authorities. France 24’s Luke Shrago has more.

events.title: Can Sweden restore welfare system amid increased defense spending?
events.summary: While the results of Sweden's general election remain too close to call, it looks as though the country's center-left opposition may get the chance to form a new government after four years under a right-wing coalition. The runup to the vote was dominated domestic economic issues, including the future of the country's once famously generous welfare state. But Sweden's international financial commitments - notably to increased defense spending following its decision to join NATO amid Russia's war on Ukraine - are likely to limit its options.

events.title: Centre-left holds narrow lead in knife-edge Sweden vote
events.summary: Sweden's centre-left opposition on ​Monday looked the most likely to form the next government as preliminary election results showed it holding a narrow three-seat lead over the right-wing ruling parties with most of the votes counted after Sunday's vote. Party leaders, however, have been cautious about claiming victory or accepting defeat with 353 election districts still to be counted ‌and overseas votes not likely to be tallied until Wednesday.

events.title: As Yemen conflict intensifies, Iran the winner?
events.summary: The conflict in Yemen intensified on Sunday, as government forces launched attacks against Iran-backed Houthi rebels along the Red Sea and Houthis fired into neighboring Saudi Arabia, which supports Yemen’s government. It comes after Houthis captured the port city of Mokha and an island on the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, a crucial shipping alternative to the Strait of Hormuz. The adds pressure on global oil supplies and prices, and that could give Iran leverage in its war with the United States. Andrew Hilliar has more.

events.title: Indonesia: Rescuers resume search for 129 missing after ferry capsized

events.title: 'State-led discrimination': Turkey detains dozens after raids targeting LGBTQ groups
events.summary: Turkish police on Sunday arrested at least 60 people in mass raids on gay bars and the homes of LGBTQ activists, in what authorities said was an operation aimed at boosting traditional family values. The raids sparked condemnation from rights groups and opposition parties, as well as the European Union parliament's rapporteur on Turkey. France 24’s Jasper Mortimer has the latest.

events.title: Who is Iran's 'influential spymaster' Hossein Taeb and does he pull the strings?

events.summary: Kaegan Jude Solet, 47, was taken into custody Sunday in connection with a stabbing spree Friday that left four people dead and one in critical condition.

events.title: Amazon suspends use of 21 Air, cargo carrier involved in fatal Miami crash
events.summary: Online retailer Amazon said Sunday it was suspending its use of cargo carrier 21 Air after one of its Amazon-branded aircraft crashed upon landing in Miami this month, killing five people.

events.title: Why are Americans so tired so often? New CDC report highlights who’s feeling it most
events.summary: About 71% of of adults in the U.S. say they experience fatigue, a new report from the CDC found. Women and younger adults are feeling it most often.

events.title: Your health insurance bills are about to go up
events.summary: Most Americans can expect to pay significantly more each month for health insurance next year, whether they get it through work, the Affordable Care Act or Medicare.

events.title: Rep. Tom Tiffany swims to safety after his plane made emergency landing on lake
events.summary: Rescue teams were called to reports of a downed plane with two people in the water, emergency services’ radio communications indicate.

events.title: China dismisses AI slowdown calls and blasts ‘fearmongering’ from U.S. tech leaders
events.summary: Urgent calls for a slowdown in the development of artificial intelligence may cite a grave threat to humanity, but China says the warnings are instead aimed at slowing its progress as America’s rival superpower.

events.title: Air Force officer recalls ‘free-falling’ after jet was shot down over Iran
events.summary: In an interview with CBS’ “60 Minutes,” one of the two U.S. Air Force officers whose fighter jet was shot down over Iran in April detailed his harrowing ordeal.

events.title: Saudi shutdown of key pipeline limits oil flow as Yemen hits back against Houthis
events.summary: Saudi Arabia has closed a critical oil pipeline after it was struck by drones launched from Iraq, with the latest squeeze reverberating through the region Saturday as attacks by Iran-backed Houthi rebels threatened to deepen the world’s energy crisis.

events.title: Strikes shut down key Saudi pipeline as Iran-backed Houthis tighten grip on crucial shipping lane
events.summary: Houthi rebels effectively completed a rapid push to take control of Yemen’s Red Sea coastline on Friday, tightening their grip on one of the world’s most important shipping routes and delivering a dramatic boost to their backers in Iran.

events.title: Chinese company releases video of humanoid robot walking off assembly line on its own
events.summary: Chinese company Xpeng released a video showing its new humanoid robot IRON walking off the assembly line on its own. It’s the latest step in the robot arms race between the U.S. and China that could eventually lead to mass production of the humanoids. NBC News’ Priscilla Thompson reports.

events.title: Iran-backed Houthis take control of Red Sea coastline in Yemen
events.summary: The Iran-backed Houthi rebels in Yemen have taken control of a strategic Red Sea coastline, further complicating shipping routes in the region. At the same time, strikes inside Saudi Arabia forced the shutdown of a critical oil pipeline, the country’s energy ministry confirmed.

events.title: Rick Springfield opens up about killing a man in Vietnam while performing for troops in 1968
events.summary: Rocker Rick Springfield recalled how, as a teenager, when he performed for U.S. forces in Vietnam, they came under attack and he killed a Viet Cong — haunting him to this day that he “was responsible for the end of a life.” NBC News' Maggie Vespa reports.

events.title: At least five dead, dozens missing after Philippine ferry fire
events.summary: The Philippine coast guard searched for survivors after a ferry carrying 134 people caught fire in the western Palawan province while sailing from Manila. Authorities said at least five people died while dozens of others are missing, adding that 42 people had been rescued.

events.title: Diesel pushes to new all-time high as oil prices jump after key Saudi pipeline is shut
events.summary: The price of oil jumped Monday after Saudi Arabia shut a critical pipeline and talks about the future of the Strait of Hormuz were postponed.

events.title: Emma Bonino, leader of abortion and divorce battles that changed Italy, dies at 78
events.summary: Emma Bonino, who rose to political prominence as a leader of campaigns by the Radical Party that legalized abortion and divorce in the 1970s in heavily Roman Catholic Italy, against the objections of the Vatican, has died.

events.title: They led vigils for victims of Tiananmen. Now they’re facing time in prison for it.
events.summary: Three pro-democracy activists in Hong Kong who organized annual vigils for victims of China’s 1989 Tiananmen Square crackdown were sentenced Friday under a national security law that critics say has stifled dissent.

events.title: Flight carrying Zelenskyy to Norway was delayed in Moldova because of drone incursion
events.summary: Moldova had closed its airspace to protect planes flying over the country, delaying three departures, including Zelenskyy’s.

events.title: Oil surges past $101 to highest closing level since May as Iran conflict intensifies
events.summary: The price of oil breached the $100 threshold as new flare-ups between the U.S. and Iran stoked fresh concern for global energy markets.

events.title: China hits back at U.S. claim its AI companies systematically copied American models
events.summary: In its most detailed accusation yet, the U.S. government has named six Chinese AI companies that it says copied American companies for their AI secrets.

events.title: Iran attacks American warships and base after U.S. sinks five Iranian tankers
events.summary: They’re the latest tit-for-tat strikes as Washington and Tehran lurch back toward fighting during more than six months of war.

events.title: Widespread flight delays hit major British airports
events.summary: Flights departing from two of London’s Heathrow Airport have been grounded following a “technical issue.”

events.title: Chinese hackers are running AI on stolen networks to avoid detection, Google says
events.summary: One China-linked group targets academic, medical and military AI research, the report says.

events.title: Harry and Meghan ‘surprised’ by king’s letter making clear they’re still nonworking royals
events.summary: A spokesman for the couple told NBC News that a government committee was meeting this week to discuss whether to provide security for the family now that they have moved back to the U.K.
